## Intake Brief: Multi-agent audit/test coordination to break deadlocks

## Work item
**SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF -- When multiple agents are working they can become blocked on audits/testing**

## Problem statement

When multiple agents run concurrently (herdr-dispatched implement/plan/audit panes plus manual sessions), audits and test runs contend for the same scarce host resources (local LLM slots, audit concurrency slots, CPU) and end up blocking one another. Two mechanisms interact to create a livelock/starvation pattern: (1) the herdr downtime worker only dispatches any work -- including audits -- after the local LLM has been **continuously idle >=60s with >=2 free slots**; (2) the audit runner **fails fast (0s wait)** when the host-wide audit semaphore is saturated, returning `unmet` "Audit concurrency limit reached" verdicts. Under sustained agent traffic the idle gate never opens, so audits starve; in the rare dispatch windows, concurrent audits may still collide and fail-fast, keeping items `in_review` indefinitely. Tableau-Card-Engine currently shows 28 items in `in_review` -- several 1000+ hours old (up to 4178h) -- with only 15 audit dispatches ever recorded and one audit running 8+ hours. A coordination mechanism is needed so audits proceed with bounded, prioritized concurrency independent of a strict "all traffic quiet" gate.

## Users

- **Concurrent agent herd** (herdr instances + pi panes on the same machine) running implement/plan/audit sessions -- they block on audits of their completed items.
- **Audit skill consumers** -- every completed/item-in-`in_review` work item needs a timely audit verdict to progress/close.
- **Operator (rgardler)** -- watches the worklog; a deadlocked herd produces no visible progress and wasted LLM spend.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No fail-fast re-queue under load (north star):** under sustained concurrent agent/LLM traffic, audits no longer return `unmet` "Audit concurrency limit reached" verdicts as the *common* outcome; when the ceiling is momentarily saturated, audits wait on a bounded queue (or equivalent) rather than failing immediately. Verification: run N >= 3 concurrent audits against a busy host; zero concurrency-limit `unmet` verdicts; all audits persist real verdicts.
2. **Bounded audit turnaround (realistic start):** an `in_review` item is audited within N hours (N to be tuned) of entering that stage while multiple agents are active. Verification: seed/observe items entering `in_review` under concurrent load; 95th-percentile time-to-audit <= N. Note: turnaround is bounded within dispatch windows; the gate-opening frequency is the hard throughput ceiling (see AC3 amendment).
3. **Idle-gate decoupling for audits (amended):** *within any dispatch window*, audit dispatch/progress no longer requires a strict continuous LLM idle window; audits proceed under high agent traffic (bounded by the host-wide audit semaphore), while non-audit dispatch may retain a gentler gate. Note: the idle gate itself is unchanged (see SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50 follow-up); this AC is satisfied by the bounded-queue mechanism ensuring audits proceed without fail-fast once a dispatch window opens.
4. **Priority ordering:** among queued/waiting audit candidates, `critical` items are audited before `high`, then age/FIFO; no item is bypassed indefinitely. Verification: deterministic ordering observed in logs/tests; the 4178h-old backlog drains.
5. **No regression to existing guards:** per-item `in_progress` claim guard, dispatched-marker exclusion, single-flight, lease/leader machinery, and test-cache read-only consumption all continue to work unchanged (see Constraints). **All related documentation updated** (audit skill reference, process_semaphore, AGENTS.md coordination section, downtime-dispatcher doc if touched). **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Single-machine scope (v1) matches herdr's current leader-election/lease model; no new network service.
- Preserve the cross-process flock semaphore primitive (no stale locks); extend semantics (bounded wait/priority/queueing) rather than replace wholesale.
- The dispatcher cannot know a work item's weight before dispatch -- fine-grained coordination belongs in the skills (audit/test) where concurrency is actually consumed; dispatcher changes should be minimal and only where they unblock (e.g., audits not gated on full idle).
- Must not destabilize working coordination machinery: leader lease (5-min TTL), 30-min check-ins, pruning, fail-closed lookups.
- Keep test execution cheap: the per-repo test cache (2h TTL) already dedupes suite runs; do not regress read-only cache consumption by audits/implement/ship.
- Respect `.gitignore`/agent-framework rules; changes to `skill/`, `command/`, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` are tracked here, built, tested, pushed to `dev` per the global workflow.

## Plan

### Feature breakdown (5 child items, 3 vertical slices)

**Slice 1 -- Zero fail-fast + priority ordering (AC1, AC4):**
- **SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L** (task) -- Implement shared bounded priority queue module in `skill/shared/queue.py`
- **SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM** (feature) -- Integrate audit runner with bounded queue (replaces fail-fast) + queue logging

**Slice 2 -- Batch drain (AC2):**
- **SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5** (feature) -- Add batch drain mode (process N items per window)

**Slice 3 -- Broader scope + research (AC5):**
- **SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG** (task) -- Extend test skill to use shared concurrency primitive
- **SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50** (task) -- Evaluate whether idle-gate relaxation is needed (research, independent)

### Dependency graph
```
SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L (queue module) -- foundation, no deps
  |-- SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM (queue integration)
  |     |-- SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5 (batch drain)
  |-- SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG (test skill)
SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50 (gate eval) -- independent research
```

### Sequencing with related work
- **SA-0MSQIA84B005NHWC** (stale-audit detection, completed/in_review): same file area (`audit_runner.py`) but different path. This item modifies the concurrency/semaphore/launch path; SA-0MSQIA84B005NHWC works on the freshness/fingerprint path. Implement SA-0MSQIA84B005NHWC first to avoid overlapping edits.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` -- `_acquire_audit_slot()` (2124), `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (134-135, 0s default), saturation verdict path (2796-2855); central place to add bounded wait/queue.
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` -- counting semaphore (already supports `timeout>0` bounded wait; may need priority/fairness or a queue protocol, plus tests at `skill/shared/tests/`).
- `skill/shared/queue.py` -- **new**: bounded priority queue module (SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` -- suite run/dedup layer; candidate for the same coordination primitive if test runs contend.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (ContextHub) -- idle gate/dispatch tiers; candidate for the audit-gate relaxation (SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50 research).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (SorraAgents), `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (ContextHub), `packages/herdr/README.md` (ContextHub), `AGENTS.md` / `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` coordination section -- docs to update.

## Related work

Potentially related work items (SorraAgents):
- SA-0MSQIA84B005NHWC -- Eliminate wasteful re-audits: stale-audit detection and cross-session audit coordination (completed/in_review, **same file area** `audit_runner.py` -- distinct concern: front freshness fast-path vs. this item's contention/queueing; sequence to avoid overlapping edits)
- SA-0MSAK2SNN005HCM5 -- Audit runner concurrency cap (completed; the existing bound)
- SA-0MSAK2P3J0065POO -- Shared cross-process semaphore module (completed; primitive to extend)
- SA-0MSGEAZMC009LHKL -- Audit skill: fail immediately when audit concurrency limit is reached (completed; the behavior this item supersedes with bounded queueing)
- SA-0MSCC02ME009EGCB -- Investigate audit concurrency TimeoutError errors (completed)
- SA-0MSAEKOQE009TEB4 -- Investigate concurrent audit fan-out causing extreme load (completed; fan-out context for ceilings)
- SA-0MSGN5OJ4002OZKY -- Cache full test-suite results for reuse across ship/audit/implement (completed)
- SA-0MSL1YS4K008HJVU -- Audit skill improvements: P1-P3 optimization backlog (open, plan_complete; watch for overlap)

ContextHub (WL-) related: downtime dispatcher leader election WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL, no-candidate cooldown WL-0MSI7DQL10016QYX, coordination-mode WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7, critical-first dispatch WL-0MT3FM8VA005XBHE, idle-gate slot requirements WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should this item (a) produce an investigation+proposal that stops, (b) go straight to designing and implementing a coordination mechanism, or (c) be an epic decomposed into investigation->design->implementation children?"
  - Answer (operator/rgardler): "(b) -- go straight to designing and implementing." Source: interactive reply 2026-08-30. Implies single feature item (issueType set to `feature`), with plan stage free to decompose as needed.
- Q2: "Where should the mechanism live -- audit/test skills, herdr dispatcher, or both?"
  - Answer (operator/rgardler): "Wherever makes the most sense -- note the dispatcher may be too late as it cannot know what the work items will entail ahead of dispatch -- happy if you have a good idea."
  - Research (Map): dispatcher-side gating cannot know item weight pre-dispatch; the contention is consumed skill-side (audit semaphore, subprocess launches). Primary surface: `skill/audit` bounded prioritized queue on the existing flock semaphore; dispatcher relaxation (secondary) only to stop the strict idle gate from starving audits. Accepted as design direction; refinement at plan stage.
- Q3: "What measurable success? (a) every in_review audited within N hours, (b) zero 'concurrency limit reached' unmet verdicts, or other?"
  - Answer (operator/rgardler): "(b) is the north star goal; (a) may be a realistic start -- your guidance is required once you have evaluated."
  - Guidance (Map): north-star AC1 = zero fail-fast `unmet` verdicts under load; start-gate AC2 = bounded turnaround (initial N=24h, tuned from observed dispatch/backlog data: 28 items stuck, ~1 valid audit window per couple hours). AC1 is achievable now with bounded-wait queueing (semaphore already supports `timeout>0`); AC2 additionally needs idle-gate decoupling (AC3) so dispatches aren't rare. Priority ordering (AC4) addresses the oldest-first fairness gap.

### Plan design decisions (2026-08-30)

- Q1 (Queue protocol): **(a) File-based priority queue** (RECOMMENDED). Answer (operator/rgardler): confirmed. A shared queue directory where each waiter writes a priority+timestamp file; dispatcher reads in order (critical>high>age).
- Q2 (Idle gate): **(b) Keep gate, rely on bounded wait**. Answer (operator/rgardler): "We cannot loosen the gate, which means b is the only option. What impact does this have on ACs? What can be done?" AC3 amended: "within any dispatch window, audits proceed without fail-fast"; AC2 amended: turnaround bounded within windows, gate-opening frequency is throughput ceiling. Batch drain mode (process multiple items per window) mitigates throughput impact.
- Q3 (Scope): **(b) Shared primitive, audit first consumer, test second**. Answer (operator/rgardler): "implementation runs audits, scoping to audit only will have limited effect." The shared primitive in `skill/shared/` is consumed by audit first; test skill extended in a separate task. A follow-up research item (SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50) evaluates whether the idle gate should be relaxed.

## Recommendations & assumptions

- **Assumption:** bounded-wait + fairness ordering on the existing semaphore is sufficient for AC1; a formal FIFO/priority queue (file-based) for AC2/AC4 is the natural extension and the core of this feature.
- **Assumption:** audits are the scarce op (tests already cached); the feature centers on audit coordination, with test coordination as a separate task.
- **Assumption:** the strict idle gate exists to protect interactive use (reserve >=1 slot); relaxation is outside v1 scope (tracked as SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50).
- **Risk:** touching audit-runner concurrency paths regresses the many hardening fixes in that file (parent-timeout, stall detection, retry/backoff). Mitigation: surgical change in `_acquire_audit_slot`/verdict path only; run the full audit test suite.
- **Risk:** queue/prioritization adds state; a crash could strand waiting items. Mitigation: flock-based no-stale-lock design (kernel release), plus item-level retry markers so no item is lost.
- **Risk:** dispatcher-side change (if taken) interacts with herdr election/lease fail-closed logic. Mitigation: keep it minimal and documented; test tiers remain.
- **Scope-creep risk:** tuning N, backlog draining of all 28 TCE items, or building a general scheduler are separate concerns -- recorded as follow-up items if they arise, not scope here.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-08-30 Plan skill (Map):** decomposed into 5 child items across 3 vertical slices. Design decisions: file-based priority queue (Q1a), bounded-wait replaces fail-fast with gate unchanged (Q2b), shared primitive scope includes test skill (Q3b). AC2/AC3 amended to reflect gate-stay constraint. Follow-up research item created for gate evaluation.

## Problem

`StatusLifecycle.require_claimed()` compares the fetched status against `"in_progress"` (underscore), but `wl show --json` returns `"in-progress"` (hyphen). The guard therefore raises `ClaimError` even when the item is correctly claimed — its own error message reports the contradictory "current status: in-progress".

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
cd /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents
python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'skill'); from shared.status_lifecycle import StatusLifecycle; StatusLifecycle.require_claimed('<an-in-progress-work-item-id>')"
```

Observed: `ClaimError: Work item ... must be in_progress before mutation (current status: in-progress)`.

Expected: returns the `wl show` response without raising for an `in-progress` item.

## Impact

The mandated step-7 guard in the plan skill (and the corresponding guards in implement) fails closed on every correctly claimed item, blocking workflows or forcing ad-hoc bypasses.

## Root cause

`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` `require_claimed()` (`if status != "in_progress":`) and `ensure_claimed()` (`if status == "in_progress":`) both compare against the underscore form. Normalise hyphen/underscore before comparing.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `require_claimed()` returns normally for an item whose status is `in-progress`.
2. `require_claimed()` still raises `ClaimError` for `open` and `completed` items.
3. `ensure_claimed()` remains a no-op for `in-progress` items (no redundant `wl update`).
4. Unit tests cover both the hyphen and underscore status spellings.

Discovered-from: SA-0MTYJ4MGO007O22W (references the completed fix SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9).

# Fix inherited_pass bypass: three fixes in audit_runner.py

## Summary
The audit runner incorrectly allows `inherited_pass` to bypass the pre-review stage block, producing false-positive "Ready to close: Yes" verdicts. This task combines three related fixes in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`.

## Fix 1: inherited_pass assignment (line ~9897)

In the `if not parent_gaps:` branch, add a stage guard so `inherited_pass=True` is only applied to children already in `in_review` or `done` stage. Pre-review children (`idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`) must not receive `inherited_pass` — they must be audited independently.

- Code at ~9897 checks child stage before setting `inherited_pass = True`
- Only children with `stage` in `("in_review", "done")` receive `inherited_pass`
- Pre-review stage children skip the `inherited_pass` branch and proceed to independent audit
- Existing `_child_content_changed` guard is preserved

## Fix 2: all_children_reviewed check (line ~4207)

The `all_children_reviewed` check currently allows `inherited_pass` to exempt a child from the stage check:

```python
all_children_reviewed = all(
    c.get("stage") in ("in_review", "done") or c.get("inherited_pass")
    for c in active_children
)
```

Remove `or c.get("inherited_pass")` — the stage check should be independent. The `inherited_pass` flag affects the verdict, not the stage blocking logic.

- `all_children_reviewed` only checks child stages, not `inherited_pass`
- A child at `intake_complete` with `inherited_pass=True` is correctly counted as blocking
- Existing exempt-child logic (deleted, completed/done) is preserved

## Fix 3: summary text (line ~4333)

The summary unconditionally appends "All children are in in_review or done stage." when `all_children_reviewed` is true. Fix this so the line is only emitted when that statement is actually true; otherwise, the summary names the blocking children.

- The "All children are in in_review or done stage." line is only emitted when all active children are actually in those stages
- When children block closure, the summary names them
- No regression on existing "Ready to close: No" cases that already name blocking children

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All three fixes applied in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- [ ] Regression test passes (separate task SA-0MUD5OMQG0068P4I)
- [ ] No regression on existing tests
- [ ] Existing `_child_content_changed` guard preserved
- [ ] Existing exempt-child logic preserved

**Key Files:**
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (~4201-4214, ~4330-4340, ~9890-9910)

# Intake Brief — Add project name to the refactor report title (SA-0MUMHH4BB000WEM9)

**Headline:** The refactor skill's human-readable report should name the project it scanned — `=== <project_name> Refactor Report ===` — resolved from the Worklog `projectName` (falling back to the project directory name), instead of the ambiguous `=== Refactor Report ===`. A direct precedent exists in the parked standup project-title change (`SA-0MTWO7HFW`).

## Problem statement

The `refactor` skill's human-readable report opens with a generic heading,
`=== Refactor Report ===`, which does not say **which project** was scanned.
The skill supports full-project scans and is launched from many different
checkouts (and git worktrees), so a bare heading is ambiguous: an operator or
agent reading the output — or a log containing several reports — cannot tell
the project at a glance. The report title should include the resolved project
name, matching the style already chosen for the standup report
(`<project_name> Standup Report`).

## Users

- **Agents invoking `/skill:refactor`** (full-project scan or session-only) —
  they need the output to identify the project so results are unambiguous when
  multiple projects are scanned in one session.
  - *As an agent, I want the refactor report title to name the project, so I can
    attribute findings without cross-referencing the cwd.*
- **Operators reading refactor output / CI logs** — they scan several reports
  and need the project identified in the heading.
  - *As an operator, I want `<project> Refactor Report` at the top, so I know
    which repository a scan belongs to.*
- **Producers triaging `REFACTOR` work items** — the report context should make
  clear which project the filed smells belong to.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The refactor skill's human-readable report heading includes the resolved
   project name, using the standup-consistent form
   `=== <project_name> Refactor Report ===`. Verified by an automated test that
   renders the CLI report for a known project and asserts the exact heading.
2. Project-name resolution order is (a) `projectName` in
   `<worklog_dir>/config.yaml`, (b) the parent directory name of the `.worklog`
   directory, (c) `Path.cwd().name`. It never returns an empty string and never
   raises when the config is missing, unreadable, or lacks the key. Verified by
   parametrised unit tests covering each branch.
3. Resolution is implemented once as a reusable helper (preferably under
   `skill/shared/`) and consumed by the refactor report; the CLI output code
   contains no inline config parsing. Verified by the helper's unit tests and by
   the refactor module importing the shared helper.
4. `--dry-run` output uses the same project-name-bearing heading. Verified by a
   test.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` (Output section), README, and any
   relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Target repository:** the `refactor` skill lives in the **SorraAgents**
  agent-framework repo (`skill/refactor/...`); this work item is therefore
  tracked in the SorraAgents worklog (`SA-`).
- Must not change refactor scan/detection/auto-fix/remediation semantics — only
  the report heading (and the small resolution helper).
- The non-JSON output must remain otherwise unchanged; only the heading line
  changes.
- No new third-party dependencies. `PyYAML` (already used by the parked standup
  project-title work) is available; if the shared helper parses YAML, confirm it
  is a declared/available dependency rather than relying on a transitive one.
- Prefer a single shared helper over duplicating the standup WIP logic; do not
  block on `SA-0MTWO7HFW` (standup title) landing — refactor may ship first and
  standup can adopt the shared helper later.
- Respect repo ignore rules and existing worktree/worklog resolution helpers
  (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`) rather than resolving `.worklog` ad hoc.

## Existing state

- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` (`_main`, ~line 726) prints the literal
  heading: `print("=== Refactor Report ===")`.
- No project-name resolution exists anywhere in `skill/refactor/`.
- Precedent (parked, **not merged**): `SA-0MTWO7HFW001N9QJ` — *Add project title
  to standup report template* — implemented `resolve_project_name(worklog_dir)`
  in `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` (reads `projectName` from
  `.worklog/config.yaml`, falls back to the worklog dir's parent name, then
  `Path.cwd().name`) and changed the heading to
  `## <project_name> Standup Report (<date>)`. The code sits on
  `origin/archive/standup-project-title` (commit `e880df6d`); the item is still
  `status: open`, `stage: idea`.
- The refactor `--json` output is a structured dict with a `summary` block; it
  carries no project identifier. Adding one is a possible follow-up but is out
  of scope here (see Risks).
- There is no dedicated refactor test for CLI report rendering today; refactor
  tests live under `tests/test_refactor/`.

## Desired change

1. Add a reusable `resolve_project_name(worklog_dir=None) -> str` helper,
   preferably in `skill/shared/` (e.g. `skill/shared/project_name.py`), with the
   resolution order in AC2.
2. Use the helper in `refactor.py`'s report rendering so the heading becomes
   `=== <project_name> Refactor Report ===`.
3. Update `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` (Output section) to document the
   project-name-bearing heading.
4. Add focused tests covering the heading, the resolution branches, and
   `--dry-run`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/project_name.py` — **new** shared `resolve_project_name` helper
  (preferred home; keeps refactor and standup from diverging).
- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — import the helper and render the
  project-name heading in `_main()`.
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — document the heading in the Output section.
- `tests/test_refactor/test_project_name.py` — **new** heading + resolution +
  `--dry-run` tests.
- `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` — *optional follow-up only*:
  switch to the shared helper once `SA-0MTWO7HFW` lands (not required here).

## Related work

- **SA-0MTWO7HFW001N9QJ** — *Add project title to standup report template* — the
  direct precedent; its WIP `resolve_project_name` should be shared rather than
  duplicated. Parked on `origin/archive/standup-project-title`.
- **WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K** — *wl sync to be run before refactor and standup
  skills* — also touches refactor/standup entry points and tracks skill work
  cross-repo; confirms the refactor-skill area is active.
- **SA-0MTSNTZOV006P79V** — *Refactor skill should run immediately when invoked
  without an ID* — established the no-prompt invocation convention and the
  full-project scan path whose report heading this change decorates.
- **`skill/report/SKILL.md`** — the canonical *end-of-session* report helper
  (rendered by agents, not by `refactor.py`). This item deliberately does **not**
  change that helper; it changes the refactor CLI's own report heading.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** "add the project name to every skill report" is a
  tempting generalisation. **Mitigation:** scope strictly to the refactor CLI
  report heading; standup is handled by `SA-0MTWO7HFW`; other reports are out of
  scope.
- **Dependency risk:** if the shared helper parses YAML with `PyYAML`, confirm it
  is declared/available; the fallback branches must work without YAML.
- **Testability risk:** project-name resolution depends on cwd/worklog. The
  helper must accept an explicit `worklog_dir` so tests are deterministic and
  hermetic (no reliance on the real checkout).
- **Coupling risk:** sharing a helper with the parked standup change could couple
  the two items. **Mitigation:** refactor ships the shared helper first; standup
  adopts it later. No blocking edge is created.
- **Worktree risk:** in a git worktree the git top-level basename is the
  worktree directory (e.g. `wl-SA-...-slug`), **not** the project name — this is
  why `projectName` from `.worklog/config.yaml` (falling back to the `.worklog`
  parent directory name) is preferred over `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`.
- **Assumption:** "project name" means the Worklog `projectName`
  (`Worklog`, `Sorra Agents`, …), with the directory-name fallback, matching the
  standup precedent — not the git remote name or work-item prefix.
- **Assumption:** the affected report is the refactor CLI's human-readable
  `=== Refactor Report ===` block (the skill's own report), not the canonical
  end-of-session report rendered by `skill/report`.
- **Out-of-scope opportunity:** adding a `project` field to the `--json` output
  for machine consumers — record as a separate work item if wanted.

# Intake Brief: Untracked skill dir from a concurrent agent breaks the full-suite collection for all agents

**Work item:** SA-0MUPDDMXB0088CMM (bug, critical)

## Problem statement

When a concurrent agent leaves an **untracked** `skill/<new-skill>/` directory
in the main checkout mid-session, the full test suite fails from the repo root
for **every** agent: the new skill's `tests/` package collides with the
top-level `tests` package (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named
'tests.<name>'`), and the skill-hygiene tests discover the unwired
`SKILL.md`. The pre-push full-suite gate therefore false-fails while another
agent's work-in-progress is present — the multi-agent testing deadlock class
tracked by SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF.

## Users

- **Agents working in the shared main checkout** — they must run the
  pre-push full suite and currently cannot while another agent has untracked
  skill WIP, forcing `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` bypasses or manual coordination.
  - As an agent in the main checkout, I want `pytest` from the repo root to
    pass (or report an actionable warning) even when another agent's untracked
    skill directory is present, so my pre-push gate is not blocked by WIP I do
    not own.
  - As a reviewer, I want real regressions not to be masked by a collection
    `ImportError` caused by unrelated untracked files, so failures remain
    trustworthy.
- **The producer/operator** — wants deterministic, low-noise test gating
  across concurrent agents.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An untracked `skill/<new-skill>/` directory in the main checkout no longer
   breaks `pytest` collection from the repo root (its colliding `tests/`
   package is excluded rather than raising `ModuleNotFoundError`).
2. The skill inventory / hygiene checks ignore untracked (unwired) skill
   directories and surface a clear, actionable "untracked skill dir present"
   warning naming the ignored directory/directories, rather than a confusing
   `ImportError`.
3. Tracked skill directories are still collected and validated normally —
   the filter must not silently skip real skills.
4. Regression tests reproduce the untracked-directory scenario (collection
   isolation, warning emission, and inventory filtering) and fail without the
   fix.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must work from the **main checkout**, where concurrent agents may create
  untracked skill directories; worktrees must remain unaffected.
- No test-collection option may weaken coverage of **tracked** skills — the
  filter is scoped strictly to git-untracked `skill/<name>/` directories.
- Must not depend on operators remembering to clean up other agents' WIP.
- Resolution keyed to git tracking status (portable, no reliance on
  `.gitignore` entries that other agents may not have).

## Existing state

- A concurrent agent's untracked `skill/machine-hygiene/` directory triggered
  the failure (it has since been committed, but the defect class is generic to
  any untracked `skill/<new-skill>/`).
- The repo-root `conftest.py` previously only armed the live-repo mutation
  guard (SA-0MUG30JSE0069JEQ); it had no untracked-skill handling.
- The implementation for this work item has **already landed on local `dev`**
  (commits `9aea9207` and `8d3e1d28`) from a prior session:
  - `conftest.py` now hooks `pytest_ignore_collect` to skip untracked
    `skill/<name>/` directories, caches the git-tracked check, and emits a
    one-time actionable warning at `pytest_configure`.
  - `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py` gains
    `tracked_skill_dirs()` / `untracked_skill_dirs()`; `skill_description_prose()`
    and `hidden_skill_names()` ignore untracked dirs.
  - `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` filters to tracked skills and warns.
  - Regression coverage in `tests/test_untracked_skill_directory_isolation.py`
    (7 tests; verified passing: `7 passed in 1.66s`).
- The two implementation commits are ahead of `origin/dev` (not yet pushed).

## Desired change

Make the repo-root test suite resilient to a concurrent agent's untracked
skill directory by excluding git-untracked `skill/<name>/` trees from pytest
collection and from the skill inventory, while emitting a clear warning that
names the ignored directory/directories. Preserve normal collection and
validation of tracked skills. Document the behaviour in the root `conftest.py`
and the centralised inventory helper.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `conftest.py` — `pytest_ignore_collect` hook filtering untracked
  `skill/<name>/` dirs; cached git-tracked check; actionable warning at
  `pytest_configure`.
- `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py` — single-source-of-truth
  `tracked_skill_dirs()` / `untracked_skill_dirs()`; untracked-aware
  `skill_description_prose()` and `hidden_skill_names()`.
- `tests/test_untracked_skill_directory_isolation.py` — regression coverage for
  collection isolation, warning emission, and inventory filtering.
- `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` — tracked-skill filter + warning.

## Related work

### Related work items

- **SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF** — *(feature, high, in-progress)* "When multiple
  agents are working they can become blocked on audits/testing" — the parent
  multi-agent testing deadlock class this defect belongs to.
- **SA-0MUG30JSE0069JEQ** — *(task, high, completed)* Repo-root conftest
  live-repo guard — the same `conftest.py` surface this change extends.
- **SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH** — Remove `skill/ralph/` directory tree (completed).
- **SA-0MRMCK0C8008ESE0** — [test-failure] `test_audit_skill_doc.py` failing
  test (completed).
- **SA-0ML8XKRV80GORAL7** — Fix scheduler `wl stats` command (completed).

### Related repository artefacts

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** broadening the filter to "any untracked file" could
  mask legitimate new tests; the fix is deliberately scoped to untracked
  `skill/<name>/` directories, and tracked skills remain validated normally.
- **Risk:** a partially-added skill (tracked directory, untracked files) is
  not covered — if observed, raise a follow-up work item rather than widening
  scope here.
- **Assumption:** git tracking status is the correct discriminator between
  another agent's WIP and committed work; verified by the regression tests.
- **Assumption:** a warning (not a hard failure) is the desired behaviour while
  WIP is present, per AC2.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed context already specified the
problem, impact, and testable acceptance criteria, and repository/git-history
inspection supplied the remaining evidence (root `conftest.py` state,
`measure_context` inventory helper, existing regression test, and the landed
commits `9aea9207` / `8d3e1d28`).

# Children of an audit-approved parent are not marked completed/done

**Recurring defect — producer has raised this repeatedly.** Policy restated by the producer (2026-10-02): *if a parent is marked `completed` and it has been audited, then all its children are considered complete.* The concrete fix requested: **when a parent's audit passes, set its children to `status=completed, stage=done`.**

## Problem

A parent work item can be `status=completed, stage=in_review` with a passing audit (`readyToClose: Yes` / "Approved by manual review") while its children remain non-terminal (`open`, `blocked`, `in_progress`) or already terminal (`done`) in a way that downstream steps do not treat as consistent with the parent.

This produces two failure modes:

1. **Stuck parents.** The ship skill's post-release close step (`skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` → `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`) refuses to `wl close --force <parent>` if *any* descendant is not itself a close candidate. Since candidates come from `getCandidateItems()` (= `stage=in_review` only), descendants already `stage=done` are always classified as "collateral", so a parent whose children shipped in an earlier release can **never** be auto-closed. (Tracked narrowly as SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP.)

2. **Unfinished children under a done parent.** A parent that is `in_review` + audit-approved while children are still `open`/`blocked` (e.g. happened in the TCE v0.1.19 release for `CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ` and `CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17`) forces a manual `wl close --force` that sweeps unfinished children to `done` only as a side effect — the state was never brought into consistency deliberately.

The producer does not understand why this keeps recurring despite the policy being stated multiple times. Prior decisions that *should* have covered it (all completed): SA-0MQIQQ164007HEAA ("Parent audit should pass when all children's ACs are met"), SA-0MQFXVJAZ004A29L ("wl close should recursively close children if in-review and audit OK"), SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F ("Audit: parent-first child pass-through"). The gap is that none of them **cascade children to `completed`/`done` when a parent's audit succeeds** — they only gate the parent's own verdict or close in-review children at `wl close` time.

## Evidence (TCE v0.1.19 release, 2026-10-02)

Five parents sat at `completed/in_review` after the release. All five had passing audits ("Approved by manual review"); the close step refused all five:

| Parent (TCE) | audit | descendants | Should have been cascade-closed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ | approved | 5 `open`/`blocked` children | yes — audit approved the parent |
| CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17 | approved | 2 `open` children + 23 `done` | yes — audit approved the parent |
| CG-0MTKMGL66004I0PC | approved | 3 `deleted` + 3 `done` | yes |
| CG-0MUEUWE8400951Z9 | approved | 2 `done` | yes |
| CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y | approved | 12 `done` | yes |

All five were ultimately closed with `wl close --force`, sweeping 50 descendants to `done` (manual remediation).

## Desired behaviour

1. **Cascade on successful parent audit.** When the audit runner records a passing verdict for a parent item (`readyToClose === true`, or the `Complete`/"Approved by manual review" status), it sets every descendant to `status=completed, stage=done` and records an explanatory comment/reason on each cascaded child (naming the authorising parent + audit timestamp).
2. **Single source of truth.** The cascade happens where the verdict is known — `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (parent audit success path) — not only as a special case inside the ship close step.
3. **Idempotent and safe.** Re-running the cascade on an already-terminal tree is a no-op; `deleted` children are left untouched; the cascade never resurrects or re-opens anything.
4. **Ship close step no longer needs the workaround.** With children already terminal, `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`'s collateral set excludes them naturally; the separate fix in SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP (exclude terminal descendants from `collateral`) should still land as defence-in-depth.
5. **No regression to the scope guard.** A parent whose audit has **not** passed must still refuse to close over non-terminal descendants (SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H). Cascading must be authorised by a passing parent audit only — never by status/stage alone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — On a passing parent audit, all descendants are set to `status=completed, stage=done`, each with a comment identifying the parent and audit timestamp.
- [ ] AC2 — Cascade is idempotent: running twice produces no further mutations; `deleted` descendants are skipped.
- [ ] AC3 — A parent audit that fails (or is not yet run) performs **no** cascade.
- [ ] AC4 — `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` closes a parent whose descendants are all terminal (done/deleted) without a refusal — covered by unit tests with injected `getCandidateItemsFn`/`getDescendantsFn` (overlaps SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP tasks).
- [ ] AC5 — Regression tests cover: passing-parent → children done; failing-parent → children untouched; parent with a mix of `deleted`/`done`/`open` children → only appropriate action.
- [ ] AC6 — Existing audit + ship suites pass; `npm run build` passes.

## Notes / related

- **SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP** (open) — "Ship close step falsely refuses to close released items whose descendants are already `stage=done`": the narrower ship-side workaround. This item is the root-cause counterpart; they should be implemented together (or this item's AC1–AC3 makes the ship-side workaround unnecessary, keeping SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP as defence-in-depth).
- **SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0** (open) — "Audit runner: pre-review child with inherited_pass bypasses children-stage block": the likely mechanism by which parents reach `in_review` with open children; fixing it prevents case 2 above.
- **SA-0MQFXVJAZ004A29L** (completed) — "wl close should recursively close children if in-review and audit OK": the original decision; cascade-on-audit is the missing enforcement.
- **SA-0MQIQQ164007HEAA** (completed), **SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F** (completed), **SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H** (completed).
- Files: `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`, `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`.
- Provenance: filed from the Tableau-Card-Engine v0.1.19 release retro (2026-10-02).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MQFXVJAZ004A29L** – wl close should recursively close children if in-review and audit OK (completed)
- **SA-0MSABZO2T004B95X** – Audit runner: make cumulative elapsed-time guard configurable (extend parent-process timeout tolerance) (completed)
- **SA-0MSQJABHZ0018APE** – Content-gate child verdict reuse in parent audits (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mskb6vja005n43f, 0mua4q431008hih0, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+179 more)
